transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2026-09-03 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 56 minutes
- Attendees: Avery Collins (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (OpalWave), Diego Ramos (OpalWave), Priya Singh (OpalWave)

Auto-summary (auto): OpalWave is approaching contract renewal; they want to add two EU regions and a committed capacity uplift for peak holiday traffic. Key blockers: security review sign-off, billing PO process, and a short perf pilot to validate latency and cost. Agreed next step: Redwood to send pricing tiers and security docs, schedule 1-week benchmark pilot mid-September.

Topics: renewal cadence, committed vs burst capacity, EU private VPC/on-prem pilot, latency SLOs, fallback policies, KMS + audit logs, pricing and invoice flow.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on — appreciate the time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Maya: Maya here, hi.
[00:08] Diego: Diego on my end.
[00:09] Priya: Priya, hi all.
[00:10] Samir: Samir from Redwood, hey.
[00:12] Avery: Cool. High level — OpalWave's renewal comes up end of Sep and I wanted to walk through the expansion ask: adding two EU regions (Ireland and Frankfurt) and an uplift in committed capacity to cover holiday peak. Also wanted to surface any security/legal gating items.
[00:32] Priya: Yep that's right. We had a spike last holiday where latency to EU customers got rough and the burst just pushed through hosted and it cost more than we expected. So top things for us are predictable unit cost, low p50/p95 latency in EU, and auditability for logs.
[00:50] Maya: And we want the option to run a private VPC pilot for EU sensitive workloads — not full on prem but a customer VPC with dedicated instances or something similar.
[01:02] Samir: Got it, that's what Redwood Dedicated / Private can cover. For VPC we have two flavours: dedicated GPU pools in our cloud region with customer VPC peering, or a Private deployment where the control plane is customer-managed. The latter has longer lead time.
[01:20] Diego: Quick question — do we need to pick one for the pilot or can we do a mix? For example: Dedicated for user-facing inference and Private for PII processing.
[01:30] Samir: You can definitely mix. Many customers start with Hosted + Dedicated for throughput and then pilot Private for regulated workloads. Mixing is fine; routing policies let you split by route or model.
[01:40] Priya: What about latency guarantees? We need p95 < 120ms for chat-ish flows, else the UX team will riot.
[01:48] Samir: For dedicated pools in Ireland/Frankfurt we can target p95 around 80–120ms depending on model size and sequence length. The big variables are model variant (quantization) and batching settings.
[02:02] Avery: I'll flag that we'll include a suggested config in the pricing doc — i.e., model family, q4_0 quant, batching target, and expected token cost.
[02:10] Diego: When you say q4_0 quant, sometimes that's been mis-transcribed in our notes as Q for zero, or q4o — don't want the ops team to mix that up.
[02:20] Samir: Yeah, sorry transcribers often mangle that, but we'll label it clearly. Also note that quantization can reduce GPU memory and cost but may slightly impact output quality — we'll show tradeoffs in the pilot.
[02:34] Maya: On security: SOC 2 is table stakes, but we need to see KMS integration details (bring-your-own-key) and audit log retention. Also interested in HSM options.
[02:46] Samir: We support BYOK via KMS and have HSM-backed key management options for Private deployments. We'll include the security pack, certs, and an ops runbook.
[02:56] Priya: Legal will want to see data residency guarantees for EU traffic — if we spin up in EU, can you guarantee logs and payloads stay in region?
[03:05] Samir: Yes that's a standard configuration; we can pin routing to region and add data residency clauses for the EU-bound routes. In Private deployments customers can keep their control plane inside the VPC.
[03:16] Diego: About the pilot — what exactly will Redwood need from us to run the perf run? We'll need to replicate production traffic shapes.
[03:25] Samir: For the one-week perf pilot we usually need: sample request traces, average/peak QPS, representative prompts, and a short eval prompt set. Also a test API key and a target SLAs doc.
[03:36] Diego: I can pull traffic from the load balancers — we'll anonymize. Expect a sample within three business days.
[03:41] Priya: Who will run the pilot? Is it Redwood-managed or do we run it against your hosted endpoints? We want minimal lift.
[03:48] Avery: Redwood will run the pilot on the provisioned capacity; our SE team will instrument the tests and share dashboards. We can give you read-only dashboards or a replay package.
[03:56] Maya: And pricing — last time the billing surprised us because the bursts were on pay-as-you-go and we didn't have a committed buffer. Can we get committed tiers with explicit burst credits?
[04:06] Avery: Absolutely. We're proposing three tiers: Standard (base committed tokens + small burst), Pro (higher commit + larger burst buffer), and Enterprise (reserved pools, lower per-token cost, and private onprem option). I'll attach a spreadsheet with exact numbers.
[04:20] Diego: Need to see the math with our traffic shape though — if your batching assumptions don't match our prompt lengths we'll be off.
[04:27] Samir: We'll add an expected per-token cost range for typical prompt lengths and include a sensitivity sheet that shows cost vs average prompt length and batching window.
[04:36] Priya: On contract and PO — procurement asks for net-60 payment and a single PO to cover committed reserve. Are there standard options?
[04:44] Avery: We typically do net-30 but enterprise customers can get net-45/60 with legal approval. We'll call that out as negotiable in the deal terms. We'll also outline invoice schedule for committed capacity.
[04:56] Maya: Competitors — we evaluated a few like OpenAI and Anthropic. The cost delta with in-house infra was close once you factor engineering overhead. The deciding factor is now operational predictability and support SLAs.
[05:10] Samir: Totally — our Dedicated and Console features are designed for that predictability: token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and rollout controls like canary and fallback.
[05:20] Diego: A bit of an oddball question — can Redwood route to a cheaper region automatically when capacity is constrained? We want graceful degradation, but legal says EU traffic must stay in EU unless we have a waiver.
[05:31] Samir: Yes, routing policies support region-first and then fallback to compatible model variants within regional constraints. For strict residency you can disable outbound fallback. We'll show the policy options.
[05:42] Priya: On SLAs — uptime and latency SLOs will be in the contract, right?
[05:47] Avery: Yes, Dedicated customers get SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. We'll add proposed p95 latency SLOs for the EU pools in the doc.
[05:56] Maya: Anything about observability retention? We need 12 months of token-level logs for audits.
[06:02] Samir: We have add-on retention options; 12 months is doable with the compliance package. We'll include pricing for that.
[06:09] Diego: For the pilot — can we get a sandbox that mirrors our expected nodes? e.g., same instance class and GPUs.
[06:15] Samir: We'll provision dedicated nodes with similar GPU types; exact instance SKU depends on availability but we'll match the compute profile as much as possible.
[06:24] Priya: Timewise — if we run the one-week pilot mid-September and it's positive, can we have EU regions up for Black Friday ramp?
[06:31] Avery: That's the plan. If pilot completes by Sep 17 and sign-off happens right away, provisioning EU dedicated pools can happen in 3–4 weeks in normal cadence — that gets you close to early November; full scaling for Black Friday we should confirm by early Oct to be safe.
[06:48] Maya: Risk: procurement cycles and PO delays. If legal stalls, we won't hit the window.
[06:54] Priya: I'm going to fast-track legal but need your invoice schedule and contract redlines to show to our CFO.
[07:00] Avery: I'll attach the standard redline and an accelerated invoice schedule option.
[07:05] Diego: A small nit — sometimes transcripts and docs spell KV cache as K V cash which confuses folks; just flag naming conventions in the runbook.
[07:12] Samir: Noted — we'll use consistent names and a glossary in the ops runbook.
[07:16] Maya: On the security questionnaire, we'll need answers to encryption at rest and in transit, key rotation cadence, and access controls.
[07:23] Samir: We'll send a prefilled security questionnaire and the SOC2 report. Also include RBAC and SSO/SAML patterns.
[07:30] Priya: Great. Anything else on the technical side?
[07:33] Diego: Just one more — fallback policies. If the EU pool runs out, can we fall back to a smaller model in-region rather than route out of region?
[07:41] Samir: Yes, auto-fallback to compatible in-region model variants is supported. Fallback is policy-driven; you can prioritize smaller quantized models first, then cross-region as last resort.
[07:53] Avery: Okay recap time — agreed items: Redwood sends pricing tiers + sensitivity sheet, security pack (SOC2/ISO/KMS/HSM notes), and sample contract redline; OpalWave provides traffic traces and PO approver details; schedule pilot Sep 13–17.
[08:10] Maya: That works.
[08:12] Priya: We'll aim to get PO path confirmed by Sep 10.
[08:15] Diego: I'll send traffic samples within three business days.
[08:18] Samir: I'll prepare the pilot instrumentation plan and share a dashboard template.
[08:22] Avery: I'll update the pricing spreadsheet and include net-60 option as negotiable.
[08:26] Maya: Also please include a short one-page runbook showing who to contact at Redwood during incident windows.
[08:32] Samir: We'll include on-call contacts and escalation matrix in the ops runbook.
[08:36] Priya: Sounds good.
[08:38] Avery: Anything else before we wrap?
[08:40] Diego: Nope, thanks.
[08:42] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[08:44] Priya: Thanks.
[08:45] Avery: Thanks all, we will follow up with the docs today. Bye.

End of transcript.
